Implementation-relevant•Peer-reviewed evidence-based implementation review•March 26, 2026

Structured tau-PET reading review translates consensus into reporting practice

This evidence-based review lays out a structured approach to tau-PET visual interpretation, validated scoring systems, quantitative thresholds, and standardized reporting—an implementation-focused publication that the prior original-study-heavy criteria could miss.

Key quantitative results: The review recommends a structured interpretation process using validated visual scoring systems rather than an unspecified positive/negative impression.

BiomarkersTau PETTauImage interpretation

Added October 14, 2026 · DOI:10.1053/j.semnuclmed.2026.02.005; PMID:41896089

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The publication is valuable because tau-PET evidence depends on how images are read and reported. It synthesizes validated visual systems and quantitative harmonization into a practical structure, but it does not establish a new universal threshold or prove that one reporting template improves outcomes.

Study design

Narrative evidence-based review of tau-PET interpretation and reporting in Alzheimer disease and related dementias, aligned with international consensus guidance and focused on visual scoring, quantitative harmonization, and structured reporting.

Key quantitative results

  • The review recommends a structured interpretation process using validated visual scoring systems rather than an unspecified positive/negative impression.
  • It describes how quantitative thresholds can support harmonized interpretation while remaining subordinate to tracer-specific validation and clinical context.
  • It proposes standardized reporting elements to improve reproducibility and prepare tau PET for broader clinical implementation.

What changed

The site now treats high-value technical reviews and consensus-to-practice papers as eligible when they materially improve biomarker or PET implementation, even if they do not report a new cohort.

Strength of evidence

Useful expert synthesis grounded in published methods and consensus, but not a formal guideline, systematic review with graded evidence, prospective reader study, or clinical utility trial.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Structured, tracer-aware tau-PET interpretation can make reports more reproducible and more useful for staging and multidisciplinary decisions, while avoiding overclaiming a universal threshold.

Field medical relevance

Useful for field discussions about visual reads, quantitative support, harmonization, structured reporting, and why the PET reference method matters when validating fluid biomarkers.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The review is relevant to studies that use tau PET as a comparator or staging anchor because visual method, scoring system, quantitative threshold, and report structure can affect the apparent reference classification.

Access or reimbursement relevance

Standardization may facilitate broader clinical adoption, but the review did not evaluate PET availability, reimbursement, reader training costs, or access disparities.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Is this a formal practice guideline?
No. It is an evidence-based implementation review aligned with international consensus.
Does it define one universal tau-PET cutoff?
No. It discusses harmonization while retaining tracer- and method-specific interpretation.
Why include a review rather than only original studies?
Because practical reading and reporting standards can change implementation and the interpretation of PET as a reference in biomarker studies.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Narrative rather than systematic review
  • No graded recommendation framework
  • No new prospective reader-performance study
  • No direct patient-outcome evidence
  • Implementation may remain tracer- and site-specific

Primary source · DOI
